message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the federal holidays in Canada that create a long‑weekend in 2023 (i.e., the holiday falls on a Friday, Saturday, or Sunday, or is observed on a Monday):

| Holiday | Date in 2023 | How it creates a long weekend |
|---------|--------------|--------------------------------|
| **New Year’s Day** | Jan 1 (​Sunday) – observed Jan 2 (Monday) | Holiday on Sunday → observe Monday → long weekend Sat 31 Dec – Mon 2 Jan |
| **Family Day** (Ontario, AB, NB, NL, PEI, SK) | Feb 20 (Monday) | Holiday on Monday → long weekend Sat 18 – Mon 20 |
| **Good Friday** | Apr 7 (Friday) | Holiday on Friday → long weekend Fri 7 – Sun 9 |
| **Easter Monday** (some provinces) | Apr 10 (Monday) | Holiday on Monday → long weekend Sat 8 – Mon 10 |
| **Victoria Day** | May 22 (Monday) | Holiday on Monday → long weekend Sat 20 – Mon 22 |
| **Canada Day** | Jul 1 (Saturday) – observed Jul 3 (Monday) | Holiday on Saturday → observe Monday → long weekend Sat 1 – Mon 3 |
| **Labour Day** | Sep 4 (Monday) | Holiday on Monday → long weekend Sat 2 – Mon 4 |
| **Thanksgiving** | Oct 9 (Monday) | Holiday on Monday → long weekend Sat 7 – Mon 9 |
| **Christmas Day** | Dec 25 (Monday) | Holiday on Monday → long weekend Sat 23 – Mon 25 |

> **Quick note:** Some holidays (e.g., Family Day, Easter Monday, Remembrance Day) vary by province. The table above lists the federal holidays that apply nationwide or in the most common provinces. If you’re targeting a specific province, let me know and I can adjust the list accordingly.
